customManagers.description: Keep both JuiceFS CE mount-image references on one reviewed release.
Track reviewed package-version arguments inside custom image Dockerfiles.
Keep custom-image build scripts aligned with their reviewed upstream base version.
Surface reviewed Flux and K3s bootstrap releases without bypassing checksum guards.

packageRules.description: LinuxServer.io images use non-SemVer compound tags. Apply loose versioning and reject prerelease, nightly, and stale Ubuntu-era tags.
servercontainers/samba uses a custom composite tag format (e.g. a3.23.4-s4.22.8-r0). Loose versioning prevents misidentification.
SearXNG publishes date-plus-commit tags (e.g. 2026.7.19-6da6eee26) rather than SemVer.
pgvector uses major-channel tags like pg16. Keep the channel fixed while still allowing security-relevant digest refreshes.
PostgreSQL major upgrades require an explicit database migration and rollback plan.

linuxserver/lidarr runs on a develop build deliberately: lidarr.db was migrated by migration 043 (flexible_delay_profiles, 2026-07-22), which dropped EnableUsenet/EnableTorrent/PreferredProtocol/UsenetDelay/TorrentDelay from DelayProfiles. The 3.1.0.4875 stable channel predates that migration and still queries the dropped columns, so it reads every delay profile as both protocols disabled and rejects every release. Renovate's `allowedVersions` rule above excludes develop tags for linuxserver, and its `loose` versioning would rank the older stable tag as an upgrade. Until Lidarr ships a stable release containing migration 043, keep this pin manual.

Kea image updates stay manual: a bot must never move the LAN's DHCP server. ISC shipped 3.2.1 on 2026-09-30 as a maintenance release of the stable 3.2 series - its own release notes state "There are no incompatible changes in this release" - and this repository pinned 3.2.1 on 2026-10-12 after primary-source review (the downloads.isc.org release notes plus the image manifest, amd64-only, built 2026-09-30, which matches the beelink nodeSelector). The 3.3.x line remains ISC's development channel ("development releases are not recommended for production use") and 3.3.0 separately disables UDP/IPv4 IP fragmentation and makes packet parsing strict enough to drop clients unless lenient-option-parsing is set - failures that only surface as devices failing to obtain leases. Rule reviewed 2026-10-12 with the 3.2.1 bump; keep disabled, re-enable only when ISC ships a 3.4.0 stable release and a reviewed upgrade plan exists.

Ubuntu Squid base updates stay manual. The maintainerr-tmdb-proxy sidecar's ubuntu/squid tag names the *Ubuntu* release, not the Squid version, so the apparent freshness gap is illusory and the obvious 'newer' tags are traps. Verified 2026-10-20 against Docker Hub, the OCI manifests and the live pod: (1) the pinned `6.6-24.04_beta` index digest sha256:6a097f68... is byte-identical to the `latest` and `edge` tags, i.e. it is already the newest 24.04 LTS build - the tag prefix 6.6 was frozen when the tag was created on 2025-11-24, and the image actually ships squid 6.13-0ubuntu0.24.04.3 from noble; (2) the 'newer' beta tags 6.10-24.10_beta and 6.13-25.04_beta target interim Ubuntu releases that are now EOL (24.10 on 2025-07-10, 25.04 on 2026-01-17), so moving to them trades an LTS base for an unpatched one; (3) 7.2-26.04_edge is not a drop-in at all - it is a rockcraft/pebble image with no /usr/sbin/squid, Entrypoint ['/usr/bin/pebble','enter'] and User 584792, which would break this pod's command [/usr/sbin/squid], runAsUser 13 and read-only-rootfs contract. Independently, every squid CVE that would motivate a bump sits in a code path this proxy disables: the ICP DoS family (CVE-2026-32748/-33515/-33526) needs icp_port, CVE-2026-47729 needs the FTP gateway, CVE-2026-50012 needs cache_peer plus a cache_digest reply, and CVE-2026-61642 request smuggling needs plain forwarded HTTP/1.1 while squid.conf denies !CONNECT and allows only CONNECT to port 443. Note for the next rebuilder: Ubuntu published squid 6.14-0ubuntu0.24.04.5 to noble-security on 2026-10-20, so a same-tag digest rebuild is the correct and safe way to pick up LTS fixes - never a tag/codename change. Keep disabled; re-enable only if upstream ubuntu/squid ships a 24.04 image whose tag actually encodes a newer LTS squid build.

K3s version bumps stay manual: this repository has no state-aware in-place upgrade procedure. The install/join helpers are fresh-host-only and deliberately refuse existing K3s state, and AGENTS.md lists a state-aware in-place K3s upgrade as an unsupported operation. v1.36.5+k3s1 additionally carries 'Bump google.golang.org/grpc to v1.83.2 for CVE-2026-84445' (a gRPC-Go xDS DoS). Verified 2026-10-20: that CVE lives in xds.NewGRPCServer's routing interceptor, and both the pinned v1.36.2 binary and the v1.36.5 binary contain zero grpc/xds, cncf/xds or envoy go-control-plane symbols, so the CVE is not reachable in this cluster's linked code paths - but moving the pin still requires the upgrade and control-plane-recovery designs (prompts/design-k3s-upgrade.md, prompts/design-control-plane-recovery.md) plus a resolution of the live-only CoreDNS hostname selector, because a K3s upgrade re-applies the packaged AddOn manifests. No bot may move this pin; a human with a rehearsed procedure must.
The finance-display API client must track the same Actual release line as the server; schema drift breaks budget sync permanently.
Flux GitRepository tags must advance together with their commits; digest-only updates detach the commit from the declared release tag.
Images pinned to a build-variant suffix (e.g. '-full') must only update within that same variant. Detected automatically via matchCurrentValue — no package list needed.
Let non-security Docker releases age before opening a PR.
Digest rebuilds age briefly but are not mixed with feature-version updates.
The download automation containers share one pod and one rollback unit.
Keep the tightly integrated Open WebUI, search, and agent images reviewable as one AI batch.
Highlight DNS, DHCP, VPN, and public-record updates for isolated live validation.
Highlight databases, synchronization, and file-serving updates for independent backup and rollback review.
Major Docker updates always get individual PRs for manual review.
